lines.text: Lesson three: trading pairs. What does BTC/USDT really mean? Let's find out.
Look at a shop price tag. Rice: ₹60 for one kilo.
It compares two things: an amount of money, and one unit of the item.
A crypto price works the same way: 60,000 USDT for one BTC.
A trading pair tells you which asset is being priced against another.
The first half, BTC, is the base asset: the thing you buy or sell.
The second half, USDT, is the quote asset: what the price is counted in.
So BTC/USDT means: the price of one BTC, in USDT.
A symbol is the short name for a pair. Many apps drop the slash: BTCUSDT.
BTC/USDT and BTCUSDT are the same pair. ETHUSDT is ETH priced in USDT.
Read the price as: one BTC costs 60,000 USDT.
USDT is a stablecoin: a token designed to stay close to one US dollar.
BTC's price swings a lot. USDT's price is designed to barely move.
That makes it a handy measuring stick for prices. But designed to stay is not guaranteed.
Quantity is how much of the base asset you buy or sell.
Think of one BTC as a big block, cut into 1,000 small pieces.
One piece is 0.001 BTC. At 60,000 USDT per BTC, it's worth just 60 USDT.
The price per BTC stays the same.
Notional value is the total worth of a quantity, counted in the quote asset.
The formula: value in USDT equals BTC amount times USDT per BTC.
Say you buy 0.05 BTC at 60,000 USDT per BTC. 0.05 times 60,000 is 3,000 USDT.
Now let the price move, and watch two orders: 1 BTC and 0.001 BTC.
BTC rises to 63,000. 1 BTC is now worth 63,000 USDT. 0.001 BTC: 63 USDT.
Both rose 5 percent. In USDT, that's 3,000 more versus just 3 more.
If BTC falls to 57,000, they're worth 57,000 and 57 USDT.
A common mistake: BTC costs 60,000 USDT, so I need 60,000 USDT to trade it.
No. 60,000 is the price of one whole BTC, not the size of your order.
You choose the quantity. 0.001 BTC at 60,000 costs 60 USDT, before fees.
Your turn. Quantity: 0.02 BTC. Price: 65,000 USDT per BTC. What's the notional value?
0.02 times 65,000 is 1,300 USDT. Well done if you got it.
Other pairs work the same way. ETH/USDT: one ETH costs 3,000 USDT.
The quote doesn't have to be USDT. In ETH/BTC, the price is counted in BTC.
ETH/BTC at 0.05 means one ETH costs 0.05 BTC.
Before you go further: stablecoins have risks too.
A stablecoin is not guaranteed to stay at one dollar. It can slip, and that's called losing its peg.
It depends on the company behind it, and on the money it holds in reserve.
And notional value isn't profit. It's just what your BTC is worth right now.
Let's recap. A pair prices the base asset in the quote asset: USDT per one BTC.
Value in USDT equals BTC amount times USDT per BTC.
USDT is a stablecoin. It aims for one dollar, but that's not guaranteed.
Check yourself: you buy 0.01 BTC at 60,000 USDT. What's the notional value?
0.01 times 60,000 is 600 USDT.
Well done! Next up: what does an exchange do? See you in lesson four.
